gen-gf-noto-serif-kannada-manrope: Manrope keeps its curves wide open and its line a single steady width. Noto Serif Kannada, with its faint upstroke and downstroke difference, earns its place when the words are big and few.
gen-gf-noto-serif-kannada-montserrat: Montserrat glides along like bent wire, its strokes uniform and its curves flooded with white space, while Noto Serif Kannada keeps a tame, literary contrast. One is bookish and traditional; the other is geometric and friendly.
gen-gf-noto-serif-kannada-satoshi: Approachable from the first line, Satoshi stands tall with a wide e and joints that never bulge or pinch. And Noto Serif Kannada earns its keep large and brief, where its medium stroke modulation can be seen.
gen-gf-noto-serif-kannada-switzer: Wiry, tubular, very Swiss. Switzer holds its c tips well apart and its bowls swell nowhere, and Noto Serif Kannada gives it a moderate thick-thin ratio and a literary, traditional foil.
gen-gf-noto-serif-kannada-work-sans: Modern wire on top of old ink. Work Sans keeps its mean line high and its joins sturdy, while Noto Serif Kannada's in-between contrast lets a longer text move along without fuss.
gen-gf-noto-serif-khmer-archivo: Editorial from the start, Archivo opens its curves outward and stands on a commanding x-height. Noto Serif Khmer adds fuller stems and slimmer links.
gen-gf-noto-serif-khmer-fs-asap: Noto Serif Khmer sets a literary, traditional tone with a dark band of lowercase. Asap follows in low-contrast sans, its open arcs and tall body height nearly matching the capitals.
gen-gf-noto-serif-khmer-fs-epilogue: Noto Serif Khmer brings thin strokes only slightly lighter than its thick ones, a literary and traditional voice. But Epilogue answers in sans-serif with curvy, unclamped letters and crossbars as stout as its stems.
gen-gf-noto-serif-khmer-fs-fira-sans: Fira Sans reads wide and generous, its marker-tip lines and big x-height never crowding. Noto Serif Khmer supplies stroke widths that shift just enough to notice, which gives the pair a literary edge.
gen-gf-noto-serif-khmer-fs-public-sans: Slight thinning at the sides of its bowls marks Noto Serif Khmer, a literary and traditional voice with a dark lowercase band. Public Sans meets it with a hefty lowercase and broad open counters, trustworthy and low in contrast.
